transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-20
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE); Priya Sharma (Redwood SE); Miguel Torres (Redwood Solutions); Lena Ortiz (CortexSearch - Head of Search); Marcus Lee (Engineering Manager); Amir Qureshi (ML Engineer)

Summary:
Quick hosted API walkthrough focusing on embeddings + rerank endpoints for improving search relevance. Customer interested in hosted offering first, possibly moving to dedicated later if latency/cost demands require. Agreed to share sample logs for benchmark and security docs.

Topics:
- CortexSearch current stack and pain points
- Embeddings + reranker demo via Redwood hosted API
- Console overview and Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization
- Security/compliance & next steps for POC

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood. with me is Priya, our solutions engineer, and Miguel from solutions - um - we'll walk through embeddings and the new rerank endpoints and show the console.
[00:18] Lena Ortiz: Thanks Alex. Quick background - CortexSearch runs a multi-tenant search platform; we index docs from publishers and also user queries, we're currently seeing relevance drift and want to improve recall + re-ranking without blowing up latency.
[00:35] Marcus Lee: Yeah we tried some transformer rerankers in-house but cost spiked; we're evaluating options: host externally or keep it in house. timeline is Q2 pilot with a production roll in Q3 if results look good.
[00:52] Priya Sharma: Got it. quick question on traffic - what's your 95th pct latency requirement and query volume?
[00:58] Amir Qureshi: Right now p95 is 120ms for search path but we can tolerate up to 200ms for heavy rerank, ideally we'd keep end-to-end under 250ms. Volume ~ 5k qps peak across regions.
[01:15] Alex Chen: Cool, that helps. Redwood hosted embeddings + rerank can do a two-step flow: compute sparse/dense embeddings via the embeddings endpoint, then call the rerank endpoint to score top-k candidates. We also have streaming and batching controls in the Console and Optimize will suggest batching windows and quantization to lower unit cost.
[01:38] Lena Ortiz: When you say rerank endpoint, is that separate api or part of the generate endpoint?
[01:45] Priya Sharma: It's a distinct endpoint - /v1/rerank - designed to take a list of candidates plus query embedding and return scores. it's optimized for typical rerank patterns and supports both pairwise and listwise inputs. small transcription note: sometimes our docs call it "rerankr" in older builds, sorry for that.
[02:05] Marcus Lee: Are there model options? we need smaller models for latency-critical paths.
[02:11] Priya Sharma: Yes, we surface curated model variants in the catalog - you can pick compact rerank variants that are quantized and tuned for low latency. console will show estimated p95 and tokens cost for each.
[02:27] Amir Qureshi: How does caching work? if we compute embeddings for docs, can they be cached to avoid recompute?
[02:34] Alex Chen: Absolutely. Redwood supports prefix and KV cache - sorry sometimes transcript shows "KV cash" - but yes, doc embeddings are cached and we recommend caching document embeddings at ingest time; Optimize can also flag high-hit prefixes and suggest TTLs.
[02:50] Lena Ortiz: Security stuff - we need SOC2, SSO, and customer managed KMS. do you have SOC2 attestation and KMS integration? we also need audit logs for queries.
[02:58] Priya Sharma: We do SOC 2 type II, SAML/SSO + RBAC, and KMS integrations (AWS KMS/HSM). We'll send the security whitepaper; Miguel will drop links to audit log retention and event streams.
[03:15] Alex Chen: For compliance we can also offer Private deployments later - Redwood Private - but for pilot hosted is usually fastest to get started.
[03:25] Marcus Lee: Latency vs cost: if we go hosted, what's the expected per-query cost for a two-stage dense embeddings + rerank?
[03:33] Alex Chen: Depends on model choice and batch size. ballpark: using a compact embedding model + a small rerank variant, we usually see $0.0008–$0.002 per query at scale; Optimize can push that lower with batching, KV cache hits, and quantization profiles. We'll include an estimated cost spreadsheet.
[03:50] Amir Qureshi: Do you support per-customer isolation for logs and data?
[03:55] Priya Sharma: On hosted we provide logical isolation and dedicated indexes per account; Dedicated or Private gives stronger isolation (dedicated GPU pools and private networking). For enterprise we also offer data residency controls.
[04:08] Lena Ortiz: Sounds good. can you demo the rerank flow with a quick example?
[04:13] Priya Sharma: Sure, I'll share my screen. so here is the Console - top-left you can pick the model and the endpoint. I'll start with a query and a set of candidate docs.
[04:30] [screen-share pause - brief noise]
[04:45] Priya Sharma: Ok, sending the embeddings request - here's a sample payload: query text, model: redwood-embed-compact-v1, returns 768-d vectors. you'll see the call is <API latency 35ms> in the dev region.
[04:58] Marcus Lee: that looks fast. is that including network?
[05:01] Priya Sharma: dev region yes, and for production we'd size regionally; the Console's right-hand panel shows estimated p95 given model and region.
[05:15] Priya Sharma: next I'm calling /v1/rerank with top-50 candidates - the rerank endpoint returns scores and top-k ordering. you'll see it returns in ~120ms with rerank-small model.
[05:35] [00:05 inaudible]
[05:40] Lena Ortiz: Is the rerank endpoint returning logits or normalized scores?
[05:45] Priya Sharma: It returns normalized scores between 0-1 and an optional explanation vector if enabled. note explanations slightly increase latency.
[05:55] Marcus Lee: Can we run batch reranks, like group queries to amortize model cost?
[06:00] Priya Sharma: yes, the endpoint supports batch inputs - Optimize will recommend batching windows based on your query arrival distribution. there are tradeoffs: larger batch improves throughput but adds latency.
[06:15] Amir Qureshi: For our 5k qps peak, would you recommend hosted or dedicated?
[06:20] Alex Chen: For pilot hosted is recommended - quick time to value and we can provision burst capacity. If you need predictable 24/7 throughput with strict p95 SLAs and data isolation, Dedicated is the path. we can run a capacity planning once we get logs.
[06:36] Lena Ortiz: How do we integrate with our existing vector store (we use OpenSearch + a custom vector plugin)?
[06:43] Priya Sharma: You can use Redwood embeddings to index into your vector store - we can output embeddings and metadata, and the rerank call can ingest candidate doc ids. There are connectors we can share; we've done integrations with OpenSearch and Pinecone.
[06:58] Marcus Lee: Any dev effort estimate to plug it in? how long for a small pilot?
[07:04] Alex Chen: With sample logs and an engineer assigned, a 2-week pilot to run benchmarks and basic integration is typical. often the heavy lift is data jacketing and anonymization.
[07:18] Lena Ortiz: Ok good. Are there any quotas or rate limits on the hosted API for pilot?
[07:23] Alex Chen: For pilot we provide elevated rate limits; production quotas are configurable and we have rate limit tiers.
[07:31] Amir Qureshi: One more, do you support function/tool calling for rerank explainability? like call out to a small LM to produce human readable reasons?
[07:39] Priya Sharma: You can chain calls - run the reranker for scores, then call the generation endpoint for explanations; we also have structured output options for downstream UI rendering.
[07:52] [08:00 quick pause - background sound]
[08:05] Miguel Torres: I'll quickly show Optimize - it analyzes token distribution, recommends quantization profiles and batching parameters. here's an example recommendation: move from 16-bit to int8 for the rerank-small model, suggests a 50ms batching window for your QPS pattern which reduces cost ~22% while keeping p95 within target.
[08:30] Lena Ortiz: Int8 - do you see accuracy regressions?
[08:34] Miguel Torres: small regressions in some nlu edge cases; Optimize will run a quality regression alert tied to your prompt set/eval harness and flag if metric drops beyond threshold. you can pin model versions and auto-fallback to higher-precision models if regressions occur.
[08:52] Marcus Lee: Great. Let's talk about data retention and logs for audits.
[08:58] Priya Sharma: Hosted retention is configurable; we can push logs to your S3 or SIEM and provide event streams. We'll include audit log retention options in the security pack.
[09:12] Lena Ortiz: For the benchmark, we'll share 1k queries and a sample of candidates, we want to measure NDCG@10 and p95 latency.
[09:20] Alex Chen: Perfect - once we have logs we'll run a rerank benchmark and share the spreadsheet with cost and quality tradeoff.
[09:28] Amir Qureshi: Any sticky notes about tokenization or pre-processing we should do?
[09:33] Priya Sharma: Normalize queries, strip stop-words based on your heuristic, but we usually recommend light normalization and let the embedding model handle semantics. We'll include a mini pre-processing guide.
[09:47] [09:55 cross-talk as people type]
[10:00] Marcus Lee: Security question - can we require VPC egress restriction for API calls?
[10:06] Priya Sharma: On hosted we can't retrofit private egress per tenant; that's available in Private or Dedicated with private networking. For hosted we support IP allowlists and mutual TLS for inbound.
[10:18] Lena Ortiz: Understood. Ok next steps then - we want pricing and security docs, and we'll send logs.
[10:25] Alex Chen: great - I'll send the pricing and pilot plan. Priya and Miguel will share the security pack + connectors.
[10:34] Miguel Torres: I'll also include a small benchmark runbook and a link to a sample notebook for running rerank evaluations.
[10:42] Lena Ortiz: timeline - we'll try to turn around logs this week, would like POC kickoff next Tuesday.
[10:49] Alex Chen: Sounds good. Any other questions?
[10:52] Amir Qureshi: Nothing from me.
[10:54] Marcus Lee: all good.
[10:56] Alex Chen: Ok thanks everyone. Recap: Alex send pricing + pilot plan; Priya send security docs; Miguel send runbook and notebook; CortexSearch to send anonymized logs by 2027-01-27. We'll schedule POC kickoff for next Tuesday tentatively.
[11:15] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "KV cash" instead of KV cache), and some product names shortened in speech.
